narrative: Material PL2__MAFC767A shows erratic working-day demand (CV=0.612) with a statistically significant negative trend (Kendall p=0.029) and highly unstable lead times (CV=0.736). The current SAP policy drastically under-buffers (SS=218 vs recommended 765) while placing ~531 micro-orders per year, incurring unnecessary ordering costs of ~$26,567 annually. The optimized (r,Q) policy raises safety stock to 765 units and consolidates orders to batches of 1,812 units (~32/year), reducing total inventory costs by 90.7% while maintaining 95% service level; the order quantity is capacity-capped at 1,812 units because the true EOQ of 3,290 exceeds available storage.
warnings: EOQ (3290 units) exceeds available storage after safety stock (1812.8 units). Order quantity capped at 1812 units.
Negative demand trend detected (Kendall tau=-0.125, p=0.029) — monitor for structural demand decline.
Lead time CV=0.736 classified as UNSTABLE — supplier reliability improvement recommended.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Erratic but predominantly non-zero demand (92.9% active days) with unstable lead times calls for a continuous-review policy that triggers replenishment on stock level rather than calendar time. The (r,Q) model optimally balances ordering and holding costs under variable lead-time demand.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is the binding constraint: the economic order quantity (3,290 units) is ~81% larger than available storage permits after reserving safety stock. If safety stock requirements increase further, the order quantity will compress below economic optimum, increasing cost per replenishment cycle.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (109 units) is satisfied by the capacity-adjusted order quantity (1,812 units); no infeasibility conflict.
